items.why: Caught in the AI stock selloff after the Financial Times reported OpenAI's annualized revenue is roughly $20 billion below what it had signaled, dragging chip suppliers down with it.
Volatility gauge rose as the Nasdaq slumped on AI caution and war worries, with the Pentagon reportedly preparing for potential military action.
Crude jumped as geopolitical risk revived; oil's spike also pressured stocks and bonds, per Bloomberg's markets wrap.
The AI bellwether slid after the OpenAI revenue revision spooked the AI trade, in line with the broader chip-stock selloff.

market_note: Nasdaq leading the slide while the Dow holds near flat; oil and yields are the market's focus.
summary: An AI stock selloff is dragging the market lower after a report revised OpenAI's annualized revenue down about $20 billion. Chip stocks like AMD and Nvidia led the decline while oil surged on renewed geopolitical tension.
